passages.title: The Map Is Not the Territory
passages.text: Every map is an argument disguised as a picture. The cartographer, forced to flatten a curved world onto paper, must choose what to distort: the Mercator projection preserves angles, which made it precious to sailors, but it swells Greenland to the size of Africa, though Africa is about fourteen times larger. Such choices are rarely innocent, yet they are seldom questioned, because the map's calm geometry lends it an air of neutrality. Colonial surveyors understood this well. By drawing straight boundaries across territories they scarcely understood, they did not merely record the land; they rehearsed the future in which it would be governed. Today digital maps promise a kind of liberation, since anyone with a phone can annotate a street or a village. But the promise is partial. The algorithms that decide which landmarks to display, and which to omit, are owned by a few corporations, and their silences are as consequential as the old empires' ink. The wise reader therefore asks of any map what a good historian asks of any document: who made it, for whom, and what did they prefer not to show?

passages.title: The Ferryman at Dusk
passages.text:
The river does not hurry; neither do I.
It has carried kings and cattle, grief and grain,
And keeps no ledger of the passengers' names.
I, too, keep none. I know them by their silence:

The bride whose bangles chime against the rail,
The clerk who counts his coins and counts them twice,
The old man holding fast his bundled years,
As if the water might demand its toll.

At dusk the far bank dims to a rumour,
And the lamp I light is less a guide than a vow:
That someone, somewhere, will be waiting still.
The oar dips, lifts, and dips; the dark leans in.

They say a ferry joins two shores. I say
It only proves that shores are never joined:
Each crossing is a small forgiveness of distance,
Repeated daily, never quite complete.

passages.title: The Keeper of the Light
passages.text:
INSPECTOR: (flipping the logbook) Forty years, and not one entry says 'ship sighted'.
KEEPER: Why would it? A light that works is a light nobody sees.
INSPECTOR: The Board wants evidence of usefulness, Mr Rao. Evidence is not the same as faith.
KEEPER: Then the Board has never stood on a rock at three in the morning. (He polishes the lens without looking up.) Last winter a fishing boat passed so close I could hear its engine cough. By morning it was gone. No ship was sighted; no ship was lost. Write that in your report.
INSPECTOR: I cannot record what did not happen.
KEEPER: Madam, that is the whole of my profession. I am paid to prevent events.
INSPECTOR: (closing the book, with a faint smile) The automation proposal says a sensor can do your work for a fraction of your wage.
KEEPER: A sensor can turn on a light. Can it be sorry when the weather turns?
(A pause. The wind rattles the shutters. The INSPECTOR does not answer.)

questions.question: Seldom ___ such courage in so young a player.
questions.explanation: A negative adverb (seldom) at the start of a sentence requires subject-auxiliary inversion: 'have we witnessed'. 'did we witnessed' wrongly keeps the past form after 'did'; the others do not invert.

questions.question: I would rather you ___ smoke in this room.
questions.explanation: After 'would rather' + a different subject, the past form expresses a present/future preference: 'would rather you didn't'. The present forms 'don't', 'won't' and 'haven't' are not used in this pattern.

questions.question: The committee insisted that the treasurer ___ the accounts before Friday.
questions.explanation: After verbs of demand/insistence (insist, demand, suggest) a that-clause takes the mandative subjunctive, i.e. the bare base form 'submit' for all persons. The other forms are indicative.

questions.question: He is the only one of my friends who ___ lived abroad.
questions.explanation: With 'the only one of ...' the relative pronoun 'who' refers to 'one' (singular), so the verb is 'has'. (With 'one of those who ...' the verb would be plural.)

questions.question: You ___ so much food; we already have plenty left over.
questions.explanation: 'Needn't have + past participle' expresses an action that was done but was unnecessary. 'Mustn't have' and 'can't have' express deduction, and 'needn't bought' is ungrammatical.

questions.question: The house in ___ he was born has been demolished.
questions.explanation: After a preposition a relative pronoun for things must be 'which' ('in which'); 'that' cannot follow a preposition, 'whom' is for persons, and 'where' would duplicate the preposition.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that has NO dangling modifier.
options: Seeing the storm approach, the boat was pulled ashore.
Seeing the storm approach, the fishermen pulled the boat ashore.
Pulling the boat ashore, the storm approached.
Approaching the shore, the storm struck the fishermen.
questions.explanation: In option B the participial phrase 'Seeing the storm approach' correctly modifies the subject 'the fishermen'. In the others the subject (boat/storm) cannot perform the action of the participle.

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect form: He said to me, 'Don't be late for the meeting.'
options: He told me that I should not be late for the meeting.
He said me not to be late for the meeting.
He told me not to be late for the meeting.
He told to me do not be late for the meeting.
questions.explanation: A negative imperative is reported with 'told + object + not to + base verb'. 'Said me' and 'told to me' are ungrammatical, and option A changes the command into a statement of advice.

questions.question: Which of the following is a cleft sentence that puts emphasis on the OBJECT of 'The manager dismissed Ravi'?
options: It was Ravi whom the manager dismissed.
It was the manager who dismissed Ravi.
What the manager did was to dismiss Ravi.
Ravi was dismissed by the manager.
questions.explanation: An it-cleft focusing the object puts 'Ravi' after 'It was'. Option B focuses the subject, C is a wh-cleft focusing the action, and D is a simple passive.

questions.question: By next June, she ___ as a lecturer for twenty years.
questions.explanation: A duration up to a future point ('by next June ... for twenty years') takes the future perfect continuous. The other forms do not link the duration to the future deadline.

questions.question: Ravi has not submitted the form, and ___ Meena.
questions.explanation: After a negative clause, the elliptical addition uses 'neither/nor + auxiliary + subject'. 'So has' is for affirmative statements, and 'hasn't' after neither gives a double negative.

questions.question: Which is the simple-sentence form of 'He is so weak that he cannot walk'?
options: He is very weak to walk.
He is weak enough not to walk.
He is too weak to walk.
He is so weak to walk.
questions.explanation: 'So ... that ... cannot' is transformed with 'too ... to'. 'Weak enough not to walk' changes the sense and the other options are ungrammatical.

questions.question: There was ___ evidence to convict him, so the case collapsed.
questions.explanation: 'Evidence' is uncountable, so 'few/a few' are out. 'Little' means 'almost none' (negative), which matches 'the case collapsed'; 'a little' would suggest a positive amount.

questions.question: We regret ___ you that your application has been rejected.
questions.explanation: 'Regret + to-infinitive' is used when announcing bad news; 'regret + -ing' refers to regretting something already done. So 'to inform' is correct.

questions.question: He is one of those teachers who ___ always punctual.
questions.explanation: In 'one of those ... who', the relative pronoun 'who' refers to the plural 'teachers', so the verb is plural: 'are'. 'Is' wrongly agrees with 'one'; 'was' and 'has been' clash with the present-tense context.

questions.question: The Greek root 'anthropo-' in 'anthropomorphism' refers to ___.
questions.explanation: 'Anthropos' means human; anthropomorphism is attributing human form or traits to non-human things. The other meanings belong to other roots (zoo-, mechano-, theo-).

questions.question: The prefix 'circum-' in 'circumnavigate' means ___.
questions.explanation: Latin 'circum' means 'around', so circumnavigate means to sail around. 'Trans-' is across, 'sub-' beneath, 'contra-/anti-' against.

questions.question: In 'The salesman's pitch convinced the investors', the word 'pitch' means ___.
questions.explanation: Here 'pitch' is a persuasive presentation meant to sell an idea. The other meanings of pitch (tar, musical level, playing field) do not fit the context.

questions.question: In 'The doctor gave sound advice', the word 'sound' means ___.
questions.explanation: 'Sound advice' is advice that is wise and reliable. 'Healthy' fits 'sound sleep/body', not advice; noise and channel are unrelated senses.

questions.question: The surgeon's ___ handling of the sensitive case earned the family's trust.
questions.explanation: 'Discreet' means careful and tactful about secrets; 'discrete' means separate and distinct (a near-homophone). 'Discretion' is a noun and 'discrepant' means inconsistent.

questions.question: The Board decided to ___ the officer for misusing funds.
questions.explanation: 'Censure' means to criticise formally. 'Censor' means to suppress material, 'sensor' is a detecting device, and 'sensure' is not a word.

questions.question: After reviewing the data, the researchers ___ the conclusion that the drug was ineffective.
questions.explanation: The fixed collocation is 'draw a conclusion'. 'Pull', 'make' and 'take' do not collocate with 'conclusion'.

questions.question: Which of the following is an odd collocation in standard English?
questions.explanation: We say 'strong tea', not 'heavy tea'. Heavy traffic, heavy smoker and heavy sleeper are all natural collocations.

questions.question: The noun form of the verb 'deride' is ___.
questions.explanation: Deride -> derision (cf. decide -> decision). The other forms are not standard nouns.

questions.question: In 'They are trialling the new software', the word 'trialling' is formed by ___.
options: conversion of a verb into a noun
conversion of a noun into a verb
questions.explanation: 'Trial' is a noun that is used as a verb without any change of form (zero derivation/conversion). Back-formation removes an affix and blending merges parts of two words, neither of which happens here.

questions.question: Complete the lexical bundle: 'On the ___ of it, the proposal seems sound.'
questions.explanation: 'On the face of it' is a fixed bundle meaning 'judging by appearances'. The other nouns do not form this expression.

questions.question: 'To cut the Gordian knot' means ___.
options: to solve a hard problem by a bold, direct action
questions.explanation: From the legend of Alexander slicing through an intricate knot with his sword, the idiom means resolving a difficulty by decisive, unconventional action.

questions.question: 'To carry coals to Newcastle' means ___.
options: to do something unnecessary or superfluous
to travel to a distant place
questions.explanation: Newcastle was famous for coal, so taking coal there is pointless. The idiom means doing something that is already abundantly supplied.

questions.question: 'She lost her keys and her temper.' Identify the figure of speech.
questions.explanation: One verb ('lost') governs two objects in different senses (literal and figurative) - zeugma. There is no mild substitute (euphemism), needless repetition (tautology) or balanced contrast (antithesis).

questions.question: 'The angry sea hurled itself against the cliffs.' Attributing human emotion to nature here is called ___.
questions.explanation: Pathetic fallacy gives human feelings to inanimate nature (an angry sea). Metonymy substitutes an associated name, litotes understates through a negative, and synecdoche uses a part for the whole.

questions.question: The central argument of the passage is that maps ___.
options: are scientifically accurate but artistically poor
appear neutral although they embody choices and perspectives
should be replaced by digital technology
questions.explanation: The opening sentence calls every map 'an argument disguised as a picture' and the passage shows that selection and omission shape them. The other options are not the main claim.

questions.question: 'They rehearsed the future in which it would be governed' most nearly means that the surveyors ___.
options: practised drawing boundaries on small maps first
predicted exactly how the land would develop
prepared in advance the pattern of control that would follow
imagined peaceful relations with local people
questions.explanation: By fixing boundaries, surveyors shaped how the land would later be administered. Nothing in the passage speaks of practice drawings, exact prediction or peaceful hopes.

questions.question: The statement that colonial surveyors 'rehearsed the future in which it would be governed' implies that their boundaries ___.
options: were drawn purely out of scientific curiosity
were later corrected by digital map providers
were accurate because they understood the land well
anticipated and shaped how the territory would later be ruled
questions.explanation: The passage says they drew lines across territories they scarcely understood and thereby rehearsed future governance, so the boundaries prefigured and shaped later rule. The passage denies they understood the land and never says digital maps corrected them.

questions.question: The Greenland-Africa example is used mainly to ___.
options: show that flattening a sphere forces the mapmaker to distort something
prove that Mercator maps are useless
compare the populations of two regions
questions.explanation: The example illustrates the trade-off in projection: preserving angles inflates areas near the poles. The author does not call Mercator useless, discuss population or blame sailors.

questions.question: The author's attitude to digital maps is best described as ___.
questions.explanation: He grants that they promise liberation but warns that the promise is partial because of corporate control. This is qualified, not uncritical, hostile or indifferent.

questions.question: The line 'keeps no ledger of the passengers' names' suggests that the river is ___.
options: careless about the safety of travellers
questions.explanation: A river that records no names treats kings and cattle alike; it is impartial. The poem shows no resentment, forgetfulness or carelessness.

questions.question: The lamp is 'less a guide than a vow' because it ___.
options: stands for a promise of continued care rather than mere direction
is too dim to guide anyone
was lit only for the bride
is meant to frighten away the dark
questions.explanation: The next line says it vows that 'someone will be waiting still'; the lamp symbolises commitment more than navigation.

questions.question: 'The dark leans in' is an example of ___.
questions.explanation: Darkness is given the human action of leaning, so it is personification. There is no 'like/as' (simile), exaggeration or contradictory pair.

questions.question: In the last stanza, the ferryman's view is that ___.
options: each crossing only partly bridges a separation that can never be fully removed
regular ferries can permanently join two shores
distance is a punishment for travellers
questions.explanation: 'Shores are never joined' and 'never quite complete' show that crossings are small, repeated acts that do not erase distance.

questions.question: 'As if the water might demand its toll' hints that the old man ___.
options: is secretly anxious about the end of life
wants to jump into the river
questions.explanation: He clutches his 'bundled years' and fears the water's toll, hinting at an unspoken fear of death. The text gives no support for the other readings.

questions.question: 'A light that works is a light nobody sees' implies that the keeper's success ___.
options: is shown by the absence of disasters and so goes unnoticed
depends on being seen by many ships
can be proved by the logbook
is judged by the Board every night
questions.explanation: A working light prevents accidents, and prevention leaves no visible event. That is why the logbook is empty of sightings.

questions.question: The Inspector's remark 'Evidence is not the same as faith' shows that she ___.
options: values documented proof over belief in usefulness
questions.explanation: She asks for recorded evidence of usefulness rather than the keeper's conviction. Her remark is about proof, not religion, personal distrust or obsolescence.

questions.question: 'I am paid to prevent events' is best described as ___.
questions.explanation: It seems self-contradictory (a job whose product is nothing happening) yet expresses a truth about prevention, which is a paradox. It has no double meaning, comparison or softening.

questions.question: The Inspector's silence at the end suggests that she ___.
options: has no ready reply and may sympathise with his point
has decided to dismiss him immediately
questions.explanation: After her faint smile and his closing question, her lack of answer shows she cannot rebut him. Nothing indicates anger, confusion or dismissal.

questions.question: The keeper opposes automation mainly because he thinks a sensor ___.
options: would be rejected by the Board
cannot feel concern for people's safety as a human does
questions.explanation: His question 'Can it be sorry when the weather turns?' shows that his objection is about human care. Cost and weather are not claimed; the Board is the one proposing automation.

questions.question: Krashen's formula 'i + 1' belongs to which hypothesis?
questions.questionHi: क्रैशन का सूत्र 'i + 1' किस परिकल्पना से संबंधित है?
questions.explanation: The Input Hypothesis says we acquire language when we understand input slightly beyond our current level (i + 1). The others deal with conscious editing, order of morphemes and emotional barriers.
questions.explanationHi: इनपुट परिकल्पना के अनुसार हम तब भाषा अर्जित करते हैं जब समझा जाने वाला इनपुट हमारे वर्तमान स्तर से थोड़ा ऊपर (i + 1) हो। अन्य परिकल्पनाएँ सचेत संपादन, क्रम और भावनात्मक बाधाओं से जुड़ी हैं।

questions.question: Swain's Output Hypothesis claims that learners benefit from producing language because ___.
questions.questionHi: स्वेन की आउटपुट परिकल्पना के अनुसार भाषा बोलने-लिखने से सीखने वाले को लाभ होता है क्योंकि ___।
options: it makes them notice gaps in their own knowledge and process language more deeply
it replaces the need for any input
it lowers the affective filter automatically
it helps them memorise grammar rules by rote
optionsHi: इससे वे अपने ज्ञान की कमियों को पहचानते हैं और भाषा को अधिक गहराई से संसाधित करते हैं
इससे किसी भी इनपुट की ज़रूरत समाप्त हो जाती है
इससे भावात्मक फ़िल्टर अपने-आप कम हो जाता है
इससे वे व्याकरण के नियम रटकर याद करते हैं
questions.explanation: Swain argued that 'pushed output' makes learners notice what they cannot yet say and move from meaning-based to syntax-based processing. She did not say that input is unnecessary.
questions.explanationHi: स्वेन के अनुसार 'प्रेरित आउटपुट' से सीखने वाला देखता है कि वह क्या नहीं कह पा रहा है और अर्थ-आधारित से व्याकरण-आधारित प्रक्रिया की ओर बढ़ता है। उन्होंने इनपुट को अनावश्यक नहीं कहा।

questions.question: Which scholar proposed that negotiation of meaning in conversation promotes second-language acquisition?
questions.questionHi: किस विद्वान ने प्रस्तावित किया कि बातचीत में अर्थ की वार्ता (negotiation of meaning) द्वितीय भाषा अर्जन को बढ़ावा देती है?
questions.explanation: Michael Long's Interaction Hypothesis holds that interactional adjustments such as clarification requests make input comprehensible. Chomsky, Hymes and Vygotsky are linked to other ideas.
questions.explanationHi: माइकल लॉन्ग की इंटरैक्शन परिकल्पना के अनुसार स्पष्टीकरण माँगने जैसे समायोजन इनपुट को समझने योग्य बनाते हैं। चॉम्स्की, हाइम्स और वाइगोत्स्की अन्य विचारों से जुड़े हैं।

questions.question: Schumann's Acculturation Model suggests that a learner's progress in the second language depends mainly on ___.
questions.questionHi: शूमैन के संस्कृतिग्रहण (Acculturation) मॉडल के अनुसार द्वितीय भाषा में प्रगति मुख्यतः किस पर निर्भर करती है?
options: the social and psychological distance from the target-language group
the number of grammar rules memorised
optionsHi: यौवनारंभ के समय सीखने वाले की आयु
लक्ष्य-भाषा समूह से सामाजिक और मनोवैज्ञानिक दूरी
याद किए गए व्याकरण नियमों की संख्या
questions.explanation: Schumann argued that the smaller the social and psychological distance between the learner and the target-language community, the better the acquisition. The other factors are not central to his model.
questions.explanationHi: शूमैन के अनुसार सीखने वाले और लक्ष्य-भाषा समुदाय के बीच सामाजिक व मनोवैज्ञानिक दूरी जितनी कम होगी, अर्जन उतना बेहतर होगा। अन्य कारक उनके मॉडल के केंद्र में नहीं हैं।

questions.question: According to Cummins, a migrant child may gain BICS in about two years, whereas CALP generally takes about ___.
questions.questionHi: कमिंस के अनुसार एक प्रवासी बच्चा BICS लगभग दो वर्ष में पा सकता है, जबकि CALP सामान्यतः लगभग ___ में विकसित होती है।
questions.explanation: Basic Interpersonal Communicative Skills develop quickly, while Cognitive Academic Language Proficiency usually needs about five to seven years. The other durations are unrealistic.
questions.explanationHi: BICS (बोलचाल की भाषा) जल्दी विकसित होती है, जबकि CALP (शैक्षणिक भाषा-दक्षता) के लिए सामान्यतः पाँच से सात वर्ष लगते हैं। अन्य अवधियाँ अवास्तविक हैं।

questions.question: A child who keeps asking 'Why?' and 'How?' to explore the world is using which of Halliday's functions of language?
questions.questionHi: जो बच्चा दुनिया को जानने के लिए बार-बार 'क्यों?' और 'कैसे?' पूछता है, वह हैलिडे के भाषा-प्रकार्यों में से किसका उपयोग कर रहा है?
questions.explanation: The heuristic function is the use of language to learn and investigate. Instrumental is for getting needs met, regulatory for controlling others, and imaginative for creating make-believe worlds.
questions.explanationHi: अन्वेषणात्मक प्रकार्य में भाषा का उपयोग सीखने और खोजने के लिए होता है। साधनात्मक प्रकार्य आवश्यकताएँ पूरी करने, नियामक दूसरों को नियंत्रित करने और काल्पनिक कल्पना की दुनिया बनाने के लिए होता है।

questions.question: Who introduced the term 'communicative competence' in reaction to Chomsky's idea of linguistic competence?
questions.questionHi: चॉम्स्की की भाषिक सक्षमता की अवधारणा के विरोध में 'संप्रेषणात्मक सक्षमता' शब्द किसने दिया?
questions.explanation: Dell Hymes (1966-72) argued that knowing a language includes knowing what is appropriate in social contexts, not just grammatical rules. The others are linked to different theories.
questions.explanationHi: डेल हाइम्स ने कहा कि भाषा जानने में केवल व्याकरण ही नहीं, सामाजिक संदर्भ में क्या उचित है यह जानना भी शामिल है। अन्य विद्वान अलग सिद्धांतों से जुड़े हैं।

questions.question: In Canale and Swain's framework, using gestures or paraphrase when a word is forgotten is an example of ___ competence.
questions.questionHi: कैनेल और स्वेन के ढाँचे में कोई शब्द भूल जाने पर संकेत या पर्याय (paraphrase) का प्रयोग करना ___ सक्षमता का उदाहरण है।
questions.explanation: Strategic competence is the ability to repair communication breakdowns through compensation strategies. Grammatical is about rules, sociolinguistic about appropriateness, and discourse about coherence.
questions.explanationHi: रणनीतिक सक्षमता संप्रेषण की बाधा को क्षतिपूर्ति रणनीतियों से दूर करने की क्षमता है। व्याकरणिक सक्षमता नियमों से, सामाजिक-भाषिक उपयुक्तता से और विमर्श संगति से जुड़ी है।

questions.question: A study that classifies learners' actual errors and traces them to interlingual and intralingual sources is called ___.
questions.questionHi: जो अध्ययन सीखने वालों की वास्तविक त्रुटियों का वर्गीकरण करके उनके अंतर-भाषिक और अंतःभाषिक स्रोत खोजता है, उसे ___ कहते हैं।
questions.explanation: Error Analysis (Corder) studies real learner errors. Contrastive Analysis only predicts errors by comparing L1 and L2 systems, so it cannot describe actual output.
questions.explanationHi: त्रुटि विश्लेषण (कॉर्डर) वास्तविक त्रुटियों का अध्ययन करता है। व्यतिरेकी विश्लेषण केवल L1 और L2 की तुलना करके त्रुटियों का अनुमान लगाता है।

questions.question: A learner who, after years of immersion, still says 'He go to office' and does not improve is showing ___.
questions.questionHi: जो सीखने वाला वर्षों तक भाषा-परिवेश में रहने के बाद भी 'He go to office' कहता है और सुधार नहीं करता, वह ___ दर्शा रहा है।
questions.explanation: Selinker's fossilisation is the permanent stabilisation of incorrect forms in interlanguage despite exposure and instruction. Code-switching is alternating languages; overgeneralisation is applying a rule too widely.
questions.explanationHi: सेलिंकर के अनुसार जीवाश्मीकरण में अंतर्भाषा के गलत रूप परिवेश और शिक्षण के बावजूद स्थायी हो जाते हैं। कोड-स्विचिंग भाषाएँ बदलना है और अतिसामान्यीकरण नियम को अधिक लागू करना।

questions.question: In the revised Bloom's taxonomy, composing an original short story belongs to the level ___.
questions.questionHi: संशोधित ब्लूम वर्गीकरण में एक मौलिक लघु कहानी लिखना किस स्तर में आता है?
questions.explanation: Producing something new and original is the top level, Create, in Anderson and Krathwohl's revision. Evaluate means judging, Apply means using, and Analyse means breaking into parts.
questions.explanationHi: कुछ नया और मौलिक रचना एंडरसन-क्रैथवोल के संशोधन में सर्वोच्च स्तर 'सृजन' है। मूल्यांकन परखना, अनुप्रयोग उपयोग करना और विश्लेषण भागों में बाँटना है।

questions.question: A teacher gives a sentence frame at first and then gradually withdraws it as the learner becomes confident. This illustrates ___.
questions.questionHi: शिक्षक पहले वाक्य-ढाँचा देता है और सीखने वाले के आत्मविश्वास बढ़ने पर उसे धीरे-धीरे हटा लेता है। यह ___ का उदाहरण है।
questions.explanation: Temporary, adjustable support that is withdrawn as competence grows is scaffolding, working in Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development. The other terms do not describe fading support.
questions.explanationHi: क्षमता बढ़ने के साथ हटाया जाने वाला अस्थायी समायोज्य सहारा स्कैफ़ोल्डिंग है, जो वाइगोत्स्की के निकटतम विकास क्षेत्र (ZPD) में काम करता है। अन्य शब्द इसे नहीं बताते।

questions.question: Lenneberg's critical period hypothesis, applied to language learning, claims that ___.
questions.questionHi: भाषा सीखने पर लागू होने पर लेनेबर्ग की क्रांतिक अवधि परिकल्पना (critical period hypothesis) का दावा है कि ___।
options: there is a biologically limited period, ending around puberty, for natural acquisition of a language
a language can be acquired equally well at any age
only children raised in bilingual homes can learn a second language
grammar must be taught before vocabulary
optionsHi: भाषा के स्वाभाविक अर्जन के लिए एक जैविक रूप से सीमित अवधि होती है, जो लगभग यौवन तक समाप्त हो जाती है
भाषा किसी भी उम्र में समान रूप से अच्छी सीखी जा सकती है
केवल द्विभाषी घरों के बच्चे ही दूसरी भाषा सीख सकते हैं
व्याकरण को शब्दावली से पहले पढ़ाना चाहिए
questions.explanation: Lenneberg proposed that language acquisition is easiest during a biologically determined window that closes around puberty. The other statements contradict or misstate the hypothesis.
questions.explanationHi: लेनेबर्ग ने प्रस्ताव दिया कि भाषा अर्जन एक जैविक रूप से निर्धारित अवधि में सबसे आसान होता है, जो लगभग यौवन के आसपास बंद हो जाती है। अन्य कथन परिकल्पना के विपरीत या गलत हैं।

questions.question: Allowing learners to use their whole linguistic repertoire (for example Hindi, Chhattisgarhi and English) to make meaning in class is called ___.
questions.questionHi: कक्षा में सीखने वालों को अपने पूरे भाषाई भंडार (जैसे हिंदी, छत्तीसगढ़ी और अंग्रेज़ी) का उपयोग करके अर्थ निर्माण करने देना ___ कहलाता है।
questions.explanation: Translanguaging treats the languages of a multilingual learner as one integrated resource. Diglossia is the functional split of two varieties in a society, and fossilisation is permanent error.
questions.explanationHi: ट्रांसलैंग्वेजिंग में बहुभाषी विद्यार्थी की सभी भाषाओं को एक एकीकृत संसाधन माना जाता है। डाइग्लॉसिया समाज में दो भाषा-रूपों का कार्यात्मक विभाजन है और जीवाश्मीकरण स्थायी त्रुटि।

questions.question: Which sequence best represents sound remedial teaching in language?
questions.questionHi: भाषा में उपचारात्मक शिक्षण का सबसे उचित क्रम कौन-सा है?
options: Punish errors -> repeat the lesson -> test again
Teach new unit -> ignore weak learners -> final exam
Diagnose the difficulty -> find its cause -> give targeted practice -> reassess
Assign extra homework -> compare learners -> rank them
optionsHi: त्रुटि पर दंड -> पाठ दोहराना -> फिर परीक्षा
नई इकाई पढ़ाना -> कमज़ोर विद्यार्थियों को नज़रअंदाज़ करना -> अंतिम परीक्षा
कठिनाई की पहचान -> कारण खोजना -> लक्षित अभ्यास देना -> पुनर्मूल्यांकन
अतिरिक्त गृहकार्य -> विद्यार्थियों की तुलना -> रैंक देना
questions.explanation: Remedial teaching follows a cycle of diagnosis, cause analysis, targeted intervention and reassessment. Punishment, neglect or ranking do not address the learning difficulty.
questions.explanationHi: उपचारात्मक शिक्षण में निदान, कारण-विश्लेषण, लक्षित हस्तक्षेप और पुनर्मूल्यांकन का चक्र होता है। दंड, उपेक्षा या रैंकिंग से सीखने की कठिनाई दूर नहीं होती।

questions.question: According to Erikson, the psychosocial crisis of middle adulthood is ___.
questions.questionHi: एरिक्सन के अनुसार मध्य वयस्कता का मनोसामाजिक संकट ___ है।
questions.explanation: In middle adulthood the crisis is generativity versus stagnation. Integrity versus despair belongs to late adulthood, intimacy versus isolation to young adulthood, and industry versus inferiority to middle childhood.
questions.explanationHi: मध्य वयस्कता में संकट उत्पादकता बनाम ठहराव का होता है। अखंडता बनाम निराशा वृद्धावस्था का, घनिष्ठता बनाम अलगाव युवा वयस्कता का और उद्यमशीलता बनाम हीनता मध्य बाल्यावस्था का संकट है।

questions.question: A 14-year-old keeps changing her style, friend groups and career ideas while asking 'Who am I?'. According to Erikson, she is facing the crisis of ___.
questions.questionHi: एक 14 वर्षीय लड़की बार-बार अपना पहनावा, मित्र-समूह और करियर-विचार बदलती है और पूछती है 'मैं कौन हूँ?'। एरिक्सन के अनुसार वह किस संकट का सामना कर रही है?
questions.explanation: Adolescence (about 12-18 years) is the stage of identity versus role confusion. Industry vs inferiority is for school age, initiative vs guilt for early childhood, and intimacy vs isolation for young adulthood.
questions.explanationHi: किशोरावस्था (लगभग 12-18 वर्ष) पहचान बनाम भूमिका-भ्रम की अवस्था है। उद्यमिता बनाम हीनता विद्यालय-आयु की, पहल बनाम अपराध-बोध प्रारंभिक बाल्यावस्था की और आत्मीयता बनाम अलगाव युवावस्था की अवस्था है।

questions.question: A 15-month-old repeatedly drops a spoon from the high chair in different ways to see what happens. This is Piaget's ___.
questions.questionHi: 15 माह का बच्चा चम्मच को ऊँची कुर्सी से अलग-अलग तरीकों से बार-बार गिराकर देखता है कि क्या होता है। यह पियाजे की ___ है।
questions.explanation: Tertiary circular reactions (about 12-18 months) involve deliberate experimentation with variations. Primary ones centre on the child's own body, and secondary ones repeat interesting effects on objects without variation.
questions.explanationHi: तृतीयक वृत्तीय प्रतिक्रियाओं (लगभग 12-18 माह) में बच्चा जानबूझकर अलग-अलग प्रयोग करता है। प्राथमिक अपने शरीर पर केंद्रित और द्वितीयक वस्तुओं पर प्रभावों की बिना बदलाव दोहराव होती हैं।

questions.question: Ausubel's 'advance organiser' is ___.
questions.questionHi: ऑसुबेल का 'अग्रिम संगठक' (advance organiser) ___ है।
options: a general introductory framework presented before new material to link it with prior knowledge
a reward given after a correct response
a summary test taken at the end of a unit
a group activity for peer teaching
optionsHi: नई सामग्री से पहले दिया गया सामान्य परिचयात्मक ढाँचा, जो उसे पूर्व ज्ञान से जोड़ता है
सही उत्तर के बाद दिया गया पुरस्कार
इकाई के अंत में लिया गया सारांश-परीक्षण
questions.explanation: Advance organisers are introduced before the lesson to provide a conceptual bridge to prior knowledge, supporting meaningful reception learning. The other options describe reinforcement, a test or peer work.
questions.explanationHi: अग्रिम संगठक पाठ से पहले दिया जाता है और पूर्व ज्ञान से वैचारिक पुल बनाता है, जिससे सार्थक ग्रहण अधिगम में मदद मिलती है। अन्य विकल्प पुनर्बलन, परीक्षण या सहपाठी कार्य का वर्णन करते हैं।

questions.question: Which of the following is the best example of fluid intelligence?
questions.questionHi: निम्नलिखित में से तरल बुद्धि (fluid intelligence) का सर्वोत्तम उदाहरण कौन-सा है?
options: Knowing the meanings of many words
Solving a novel pattern problem for the first time
optionsHi: ऐतिहासिक घटनाओं की तिथियाँ याद करना
पहली बार एक नई पैटर्न-समस्या हल करना
questions.explanation: Fluid intelligence (Cattell) is the capacity to reason and solve new problems independent of prior knowledge. The other options depend on accumulated learning, i.e. crystallised intelligence.
questions.explanationHi: कैटल की तरल बुद्धि पूर्व ज्ञान से स्वतंत्र होकर तर्क करने और नई समस्याएँ हल करने की क्षमता है। अन्य विकल्प संचित सीख पर निर्भर हैं, यानी क्रिस्टलित बुद्धि।

questions.question: Asking students to list as many uses of a brick as they can think of mainly measures ___ (Guilford).
questions.questionHi: विद्यार्थियों से ईंट के अधिक से अधिक उपयोग बताने को कहना मुख्यतः ___ (गिल्फ़ोर्ड) को मापता है।
questions.explanation: Generating many varied responses to an open-ended prompt is divergent thinking, a core component of creativity. Convergent thinking seeks a single correct answer.
questions.explanationHi: खुले प्रश्न पर अनेक भिन्न उत्तर देना अपसारी चिंतन है, जो सृजनात्मकता का मूल घटक है। अभिसारी चिंतन में एक ही सही उत्तर खोजा जाता है।

questions.question: Correlating the scores on the odd-numbered and even-numbered items of the same test estimates which type of reliability?
questions.questionHi: एक ही परीक्षण के विषम और सम प्रश्नों के प्राप्तांकों का सह-संबंध निकालने से किस प्रकार की विश्वसनीयता का आकलन होता है?
questions.explanation: Splitting one test into two halves (odd-even) and correlating them gives split-half reliability (internal consistency). Test-retest needs two administrations, parallel forms need two versions, and inter-rater compares scorers.
questions.explanationHi: एक परीक्षण को दो भागों (विषम-सम) में बाँटकर सह-संबंध निकालना अर्ध-विभाजन विश्वसनीयता (आंतरिक संगति) देता है। टेस्ट-रीटेस्ट में दो बार परीक्षण, समानांतर रूप में दो रूप और अंतर-मूल्यांकनकर्ता में अंक देने वालों की तुलना होती है।

questions.question: If more students of the low-scoring group than of the high-scoring group answer an item correctly, the item has ___.
questions.questionHi: यदि किसी प्रश्न का सही उत्तर उच्च-प्राप्तांक समूह की तुलना में निम्न-प्राप्तांक समूह के अधिक विद्यार्थी देते हैं, तो उस प्रश्न में ___ है।
questions.explanation: A good item is answered correctly by more high scorers (positive discrimination). When low scorers do better, the discrimination index is negative and the item should be revised or dropped.
questions.explanationHi: अच्छे प्रश्न का सही उत्तर अधिक उच्च-प्राप्तांक वाले देते हैं (धनात्मक विभेदन)। जब निम्न वाले बेहतर करते हैं तो विभेदन सूचकांक ऋणात्मक होता है और प्रश्न बदलना या हटाना चाहिए।

questions.question: Declaring a learner 'competent' because she scored 80 per cent or above, irrespective of how others scored, is an example of ___.
questions.questionHi: किसी विद्यार्थी को 'सक्षम' घोषित करना क्योंकि उसने 80 प्रतिशत या अधिक अंक पाए, चाहे दूसरों के अंक कुछ भी हों, ___ का उदाहरण है।
questions.explanation: Criterion-referenced assessment compares performance with a fixed standard. Norm-referenced and percentile methods compare a learner with other learners.
questions.explanationHi: कसौटी-संदर्भित आकलन में प्रदर्शन की तुलना पूर्व-निर्धारित मानक से होती है। मानक-संदर्भित और प्रतिशतक विधियाँ विद्यार्थी की तुलना अन्य विद्यार्थियों से करती हैं।

questions.question: Preparing a blueprint so that test items sample all content areas in proportion to their importance mainly improves ___.
questions.questionHi: ऐसा ब्लू-प्रिंट बनाना जिससे प्रश्न सभी विषय-क्षेत्रों का उनके महत्व के अनुपात में प्रतिनिधित्व करें, मुख्यतः ___ को बढ़ाता है।
questions.explanation: Content validity is the extent to which items represent the whole syllabus; a blueprint ensures this. Predictive validity concerns forecasting future performance.
questions.explanationHi: विषयवस्तु वैधता यह है कि प्रश्न पूरे पाठ्यक्रम का कितना प्रतिनिधित्व करते हैं; ब्लू-प्रिंट इसे सुनिश्चित करता है। भविष्यवाणी वैधता भावी प्रदर्शन के पूर्वानुमान से जुड़ी है।

questions.question: Under NEP 2020, PARAKH has been proposed as ___.
questions.questionHi: NEP 2020 के अंतर्गत PARAKH को ___ के रूप में प्रस्तावित किया गया है।
options: a scholarship scheme for rural girls
a national assessment centre to set norms and standards for assessment
a board for approving school textbooks
optionsHi: ग्रामीण बालिकाओं के लिए छात्रवृत्ति योजना
मूल्यांकन के मानदंड और मानक तय करने वाला राष्ट्रीय मूल्यांकन केंद्र
स्कूली पाठ्यपुस्तकों को मंज़ूरी देने वाला बोर्ड
questions.explanation: NEP 2020 proposed PARAKH as a national assessment centre that sets norms, standards and guidelines for assessment across school boards. It is not a teacher test, scholarship or textbook board.
questions.explanationHi: NEP 2020 ने PARAKH को राष्ट्रीय मूल्यांकन केंद्र के रूप में प्रस्तावित किया, जो स्कूल बोर्डों के लिए मूल्यांकन के मानदंड और मानक तय करता है। यह शिक्षक परीक्षा, छात्रवृत्ति या पाठ्यपुस्तक बोर्ड नहीं है।

questions.question: In the constructivist 5E model, students apply the learnt concept to a new situation during the ___ phase.
questions.questionHi: रचनावादी 5E मॉडल में विद्यार्थी सीखी हुई अवधारणा को नई परिस्थिति में ___ चरण में लागू करते हैं।
questions.explanation: Elaborate extends and applies the concept to new contexts. Engage arouses curiosity, Explain formalises the concept, and Evaluate checks understanding.
questions.explanationHi: विस्तार चरण में अवधारणा को नए संदर्भों में लागू किया जाता है। रुचि जगाना जिज्ञासा पैदा करता है, व्याख्या अवधारणा स्पष्ट करती है और मूल्यांकन समझ की जाँच करता है।

questions.question: Which of the following is the best-written lesson objective?
questions.questionHi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा पाठ-उद्देश्य सबसे अच्छी तरह लिखा गया है?
options: Learners will be able to write a five-sentence descriptive paragraph on 'My School' using at least three adjectives
optionsHi: विद्यार्थियों में लेखन के प्रति प्रेम जगाना
विद्यार्थी 'मेरा विद्यालय' पर कम से कम तीन विशेषणों का उपयोग करते हुए पाँच वाक्यों का वर्णनात्मक अनुच्छेद लिख सकेंगे
विद्यार्थियों को अनुच्छेद समझने में सहायता करना
questions.explanation: A good objective is learner-centred, specific and measurable, as in option C. The others describe the teacher's activity or vague, unobservable outcomes.
questions.explanationHi: अच्छा उद्देश्य विद्यार्थी-केंद्रित, विशिष्ट और मापनीय होता है, जैसा विकल्प C में है। अन्य विकल्प शिक्षक की गतिविधि या अस्पष्ट, अप्रेक्षणीय परिणाम बताते हैं।

questions.question: In a constructivist classroom, the teacher's main role is that of ___.
questions.questionHi: रचनावादी कक्षा में शिक्षक की मुख्य भूमिका ___ की होती है।
options: a facilitator who designs experiences for learners to build understanding
a strict supervisor who permits no talk
a judge who only ranks learners
optionsHi: सुविधादाता की, जो विद्यार्थियों के लिए समझ बनाने वाले अनुभव रचता है
कठोर पर्यवेक्षक की, जो बोलने नहीं देता
न्यायाधीश की, जो केवल रैंक देता है
questions.explanation: Constructivism holds that learners actively build knowledge, so the teacher guides and creates meaningful experiences. Transmission, silence and ranking belong to traditional approaches.
questions.explanationHi: रचनावाद के अनुसार विद्यार्थी स्वयं ज्ञान का निर्माण करते हैं, इसलिए शिक्षक मार्गदर्शन करता है और सार्थक अनुभव रचता है। प्रसारण, चुप्पी और रैंकिंग परंपरागत उपागम के हैं।

questions.question: A teacher always asks boys to answer questions and girls to distribute notebooks. This best illustrates ___.
questions.questionHi: शिक्षक हमेशा लड़कों से प्रश्नों के उत्तर पूछता है और लड़कियों से कॉपियाँ बाँटने को कहता है। यह सर्वोत्तम रूप से ___ को दर्शाता है।
options: the hidden curriculum reinforcing gender stereotypes
optionsHi: छिपा पाठ्यक्रम (hidden curriculum) जो लैंगिक रूढ़ियों को मज़बूत करता है
questions.explanation: Unplanned messages conveyed through everyday teacher behaviour that assign different roles to boys and girls form a hidden curriculum that strengthens stereotypes. The other options are not described by this behaviour.
questions.explanationHi: शिक्षक के रोज़ के व्यवहार से लड़के-लड़कियों को अलग भूमिकाएँ मिलना बिना योजना का छिपा पाठ्यक्रम है जो रूढ़ियाँ मज़बूत करता है। अन्य विकल्प इस व्यवहार से मेल नहीं खाते।

questions.question: 'परोपकार' का सही संधि-विच्छेद है -
questions.explanation: पर + उपकार में 'अ' और 'उ' मिलकर 'ओ' बनते हैं, यह गुण संधि है। अन्य विच्छेद शब्द के अर्थ और ध्वनि-नियम से मेल नहीं खाते।

questions.question: 'यथाशक्ति' में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.explanation: 'यथा' (अव्यय) पहले पद के रूप में आया है और 'शक्ति के अनुसार' अर्थ देता है। इसलिए यह अव्ययीभाव समास है; अन्य समासों के लक्षण यहाँ नहीं हैं।

questions.question: 'अंधे के हाथ बटेर लगना' मुहावरे का अर्थ है -
questions.explanation: इस मुहावरे का अर्थ है बिना योग्यता या प्रयास के अचानक कोई बहुमूल्य चीज़ मिल जाना। शेष अर्थ मुहावरे से संबंधित नहीं हैं।

questions.question: 'अनल' और 'अनिल' शब्दों के अर्थ क्रमशः हैं -
questions.explanation: 'अनल' का अर्थ अग्नि और 'अनिल' का अर्थ वायु है। ये श्रुतिसम (लगभग समान सुनाई देने वाले) भिन्नार्थक शब्द हैं।

questions.question: 'माँ ने बच्चे के लिए खिलौना खरीदा।' इस वाक्य में 'बच्चे के लिए' में कौन-सा कारक है?
questions.explanation: जिसके लिए कोई कार्य किया जाए या वस्तु दी जाए, उसमें सम्प्रदान कारक होता है; 'के लिए' इसका चिह्न है। कर्म का चिह्न 'को', करण का 'से/द्वारा' और अपादान का 'से' (अलग होना) है।

questions.question: One word for 'the killing of one's own brother or sister' is ___.
questions.explanation: Fratricide is killing a sibling. Patricide is killing a father, regicide a king, and matricide a mother.

questions.question: The thief was convicted ___ robbery.
questions.explanation: The verb 'convict' takes 'of': convicted of a crime. The other prepositions are not used with it.

questions.question: Find the part with an error: 'The manager, along with his assistants, have decided to postpone the meeting.'
options: The manager, along with his assistants,
questions.explanation: 'Along with his assistants' does not change the subject, which is the singular 'The manager'; so the verb should be 'has decided'.

questions.question: 'To rest on one's laurels' means ___.
options: to be satisfied with past achievements and make no further effort
questions.explanation: Laurels symbolise victory; resting on them means relying on earlier success instead of continuing to strive.

questions.question: One word for 'a person who can use both hands with equal skill':
questions.explanation: 'Ambidextrous' means able to use both hands equally well. 'Amphibious' refers to living on land and in water, 'ambivalent' to mixed feelings, and 'ambiguous' to double meaning.

questions.question: Find the next number: 2, 3, 5, 9, 17, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 1, 2, 4, 8, so the next difference is 16: 17 + 16 = 33.

questions.question: If MOTHER is coded as LNSGDQ, how will FATHER be coded?
questions.questionHi: यदि MOTHER को LNSGDQ लिखा जाता है, तो FATHER को कैसे लिखा जाएगा?
questions.explanation: Each letter is moved one place back: F->E, A->Z, T->S, H->G, E->D, R->Q, giving EZSGDQ. GBUIFS moves each letter forward.
questions.explanationHi: प्रत्येक अक्षर एक स्थान पीछे है: F->E, A->Z, T->S, H->G, E->D, R->Q, इसलिए EZSGDQ। GBUIFS में अक्षर आगे बढ़ाए गए हैं।

questions.question: In a row of 40 students, Ravi is 12th from the left end and Sunil is 15th from the right end. How many students are between them?
questions.questionHi: 40 विद्यार्थियों की एक पंक्ति में रवि बाएँ सिरे से 12वाँ और सुनील दाएँ सिरे से 15वाँ है। उन दोनों के बीच कितने विद्यार्थी हैं?
questions.explanation: Sunil is 40 - 15 + 1 = 26th from the left. Students between = 26 - 12 - 1 = 13.

questions.question: Statements: All pens are books. Some books are cups. No cup is a table. Conclusions: I. Some books are not tables. II. No pen is a table. Which follows?
questions.questionHi: कथन: सभी पेन किताबें हैं। कुछ किताबें कप हैं। कोई कप मेज़ नहीं है। निष्कर्ष: I. कुछ किताबें मेज़ नहीं हैं। II. कोई पेन मेज़ नहीं है। कौन-सा निष्कर्ष अनुसरण करता है?
questions.explanation: 'Some books are cups' and 'No cup is a table' give 'Some books are not tables' (I follows). Nothing links pens to cups or tables, so II is not certain.
questions.explanationHi: 'कुछ किताबें कप हैं' और 'कोई कप मेज़ नहीं' से 'कुछ किताबें मेज़ नहीं हैं' निकलता है (I सही)। पेन का संबंध कप या मेज़ से नहीं जुड़ता, इसलिए II निश्चित नहीं।

questions.question: A man walks 12 m north, turns right and walks 9 m. How far is he from the starting point?
questions.questionHi: एक व्यक्ति 12 मीटर उत्तर चलता है, फिर दाएँ मुड़कर 9 मीटर चलता है। वह प्रारंभिक बिंदु से कितनी दूरी पर है?
questions.explanation: The path forms a right angle, so distance = sqrt(12^2 + 9^2) = sqrt(225) = 15 m.
questions.explanationHi: मार्ग समकोण बनाता है, अतः दूरी = sqrt(12^2 + 9^2) = sqrt(225) = 15 मी.

questions.question: In MS Excel, a cell reference such as $A$1 is called a(n) ___ reference.
questions.questionHi: MS Excel में $A$1 जैसा सेल संदर्भ ___ संदर्भ कहलाता है।
questions.explanation: The dollar signs fix both column and row, so the reference does not change when copied. Relative changes on copying; mixed fixes only one of row/column.
questions.explanationHi: डॉलर चिह्न स्तंभ और पंक्ति दोनों को स्थिर कर देते हैं, इसलिए कॉपी करने पर संदर्भ नहीं बदलता। सापेक्ष संदर्भ बदलता है और मिश्रित में केवल एक स्थिर होता है।

questions.question: If cell A1 contains the text 'EDUCATION', what will =MID(A1,3,4) return?
questions.questionHi: यदि सेल A1 में पाठ 'EDUCATION' है, तो =MID(A1,3,4) क्या लौटाएगा?
questions.explanation: MID(text, start, count) starts at character 3 (U) and takes 4 characters: U-C-A-T, giving 'UCAT'. 'EDUC' would be LEFT(A1,4), and the others start at the wrong position.
questions.explanationHi: MID(text, start, count) तीसरे अक्षर (U) से शुरू होकर 4 अक्षर लेता है: U-C-A-T, यानी 'UCAT'। 'EDUC' LEFT(A1,4) से मिलता, बाकी गलत स्थान से शुरू होते हैं।

questions.question: Which protocol automatically assigns IP addresses to devices on a network?
questions.questionHi: कौन-सा प्रोटोकॉल नेटवर्क के उपकरणों को IP पते अपने-आप देता है?
questions.explanation: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) leases IP addresses to devices automatically. DNS resolves names to addresses, FTP transfers files and SMTP sends email.
questions.explanationHi: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) उपकरणों को स्वचालित रूप से IP पते देता है। DNS नामों को पतों में बदलता है, FTP फ़ाइलें भेजता है और SMTP ईमेल भेजता है।

questions.question: A self-replicating malicious program that spreads across networks without attaching to a host file is called a ___.
questions.questionHi: जो दुर्भावनापूर्ण प्रोग्राम किसी होस्ट फ़ाइल से जुड़े बिना खुद की प्रतियाँ बनाकर नेटवर्क में फैलता है, उसे ___ कहते हैं।
questions.explanation: A worm replicates itself and spreads on its own through networks. A Trojan disguises itself as useful software, spyware secretly gathers information, and adware displays ads.
questions.explanationHi: वर्म स्वयं की प्रतियाँ बनाकर नेटवर्क से अपने-आप फैलता है। ट्रोजन उपयोगी सॉफ़्टवेयर का वेश धारण करता है, स्पाईवेयर चुपचाप जानकारी जुटाता है और एडवेयर विज्ञापन दिखाता है।

questions.question: Using Google Docs through a web browser is an example of which cloud service model?
questions.questionHi: वेब ब्राउज़र में Google Docs का उपयोग किस क्लाउड सेवा मॉडल का उदाहरण है?
questions.explanation: Software as a Service delivers ready-to-use applications over the internet. IaaS gives infrastructure and PaaS a development platform; 'private cloud' is a deployment type, not a service model.
questions.explanationHi: SaaS में तैयार एप्लिकेशन इंटरनेट पर मिलते हैं। IaaS अवसंरचना और PaaS विकास-मंच देता है; 'निजी क्लाउड' तैनाती का प्रकार है, सेवा मॉडल नहीं।

questions.question: The Eleventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution, added by the 73rd Amendment, lists subjects for ___.
questions.questionHi: भारतीय संविधान की ग्यारहवीं अनुसूची, जो 73वें संशोधन से जोड़ी गई, ___ के विषयों की सूची देती है।
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment (1992) added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule with 29 subjects for Panchayats. Municipalities are covered by the Twelfth Schedule (74th Amendment), and languages by the Eighth Schedule.
questions.explanationHi: 73वें संशोधन (1992) ने भाग IX और ग्यारहवीं अनुसूची जोड़ी, जिसमें पंचायतों के 29 विषय हैं। नगरपालिकाएँ बारहवीं अनुसूची (74वाँ संशोधन) और भाषाएँ आठवीं अनुसूची में हैं।

questions.question: The Poona Pact of 1932 was signed between ___.
questions.questionHi: 1932 का पूना समझौता किनके बीच हुआ था?
questions.explanation: The Poona Pact settled the issue of separate electorates for the Depressed Classes, replacing them with reserved seats, between Gandhi and B. R. Ambedkar. The other pairs were not parties to it.
questions.explanationHi: पूना समझौता गांधी और बी. आर. अंबेडकर के बीच हुआ, जिसमें दलित वर्गों के पृथक निर्वाचन की जगह आरक्षित सीटें तय हुईं। अन्य जोड़े इसके पक्षकार नहीं थे।

questions.question: The Bhoramdeo temple, known as the 'Khajuraho of Chhattisgarh', was built by the ___ dynasty.
questions.questionHi: 'छत्तीसगढ़ का खजुराहो' कहलाने वाला भोरमदेव मंदिर ___ वंश ने बनवाया था।
questions.explanation: Bhoramdeo temple (Kabirdham district) was built around the 11th century by Nagvanshi king Gopaldeva. Kalchuris, Kakatiyas and Haihayas ruled other phases or regions.
questions.explanationHi: भोरमदेव मंदिर (कबीरधाम जिला) लगभग 11वीं सदी में नागवंशी राजा गोपालदेव ने बनवाया। कलचुरि, काकतीय और हैहय अन्य काल या क्षेत्रों के शासक थे।

questions.question: The working principle of an optical fibre is ___.
questions.questionHi: ऑप्टिकल फ़ाइबर का कार्य-सिद्धांत ___ है।
questions.explanation: Light entering the core hits the core-cladding boundary beyond the critical angle and is totally internally reflected again and again along the fibre. The other phenomena do not guide light this way.
questions.explanationHi: कोर में गया प्रकाश कोर-क्लैडिंग सतह पर क्रांतिक कोण से अधिक कोण पर टकराकर बार-बार पूर्ण आंतरिक परावर्तित होता है। अन्य घटनाएँ प्रकाश को इस प्रकार नहीं ले जातीं।

questions.question: The rate at which the RBI borrows money from commercial banks for the short term is called the ___.
questions.questionHi: जिस दर पर RBI वाणिज्यिक बैंकों से अल्पकाल के लिए धन उधार लेता है, उसे ___ कहते हैं।
questions.explanation: Reverse repo is the rate at which banks park surplus funds with the RBI, i.e. the RBI borrows. Repo is the rate at which the RBI lends; bank rate is its long-term lending rate; CRR is a reserve requirement, not a rate of borrowing.
questions.explanationHi: रिवर्स रेपो वह दर है जिस पर बैंक अधिशेष धन RBI के पास रखते हैं, यानी RBI उधार लेता है। रेपो पर RBI उधार देता है; बैंक दर दीर्घकालिक ऋण दर है; CRR आरक्षित अनुपात है।
